rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for the Sun as the star closest to Earth.

example.english: The sun is the star closest to Earth.
example.traditional: 太陽係離地球最近嘅恆星。
example.jyutping: taai3 joeng4 hai6 lei4 dei6 kau4 zeoi3 gan6 ge3 hang4 sing1

rows.note: Use this colloquial form for the visible sun in everyday talk, especially its heat or position.

example.english: The sun is really strong today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 go3 jat6 tau4 hou2 maang5

rows.note: Use 太陽 as the all-purpose noun for the astronomical sun.

example.english: The sun is really strong right now.
example.jyutping: taai3 joeng4 ji4 gaa1 hou2 maang5

rows.note: Use 日頭 in casual speech when referring to the sun overhead, especially in weather or daylight contexts.

example.english: The sun is really strong today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 go3 jat6 tau4 hou2 saai3

rows.note: Use 陽光 for the sunlight or sunshine itself rather than the sun as a celestial body.

example.english: The room gets plenty of sun.
example.jyutping: gaan1 fong2 jau5 cung1 zuk1 ge3 joeng4 gwong1
